name: coordinator-feedback-routing
body:
Design decisions for the coordinator-mediated feedback cycle [with user]:

1. The reviewer keeps the terminal resolve/reject. Only the action step moves: the closed cycle is reviewer attaches (`open`) → the coordinator dispatches one writer per item and actions the item (`actioned`) → reviewer resolves (terminal) or rejects (reopen). Reviewers never action; writers never action.
2. Every writer is read-only on feedback: the spec-writer, the plan-writer, the implementer, and every test-implementer the agent-builder scaffolds hold no `apg_review_action`; they hold a read-only feedback channel (`apg_review`) and return an ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim to the coordinator. (Judgment call: "read-only" is read as granting the read channel `apg_review`; flagged to the human.)
3. One item per dispatch: the coordinator never batches feedback into a single writer dispatch.
4. The coordinator's review of the claim is shallow consistency, not correctness: ACTIONED with no change / WONT-FIX with changes is a mismatch → re-dispatch; a consistent claim → action it.
5. The coordinator gains `apg_review_action` (it had `apg_review` only); the reviewers are unchanged (add/resolve/reject).

Relationship to `requirements.requirement.review-surface-unchanged`: this change does NOT alter the `apg review` subcommand surface (`add|action|resolve|reject|list`) — only the agent grants and the prompt/tool prose that drive it. The two are consistent, not conflicting.

Anchoring: the durable delivered artifact is the embedded text plus its install path, not the repo-tree source file. The agent prompts and suite tool text are `include_str!` constants compiled into the binary and written to the user-level suite by `apg.install_suite`, so the `implemented-by` edges point at the install/embed Rust (`apg.install_suite`, `apg.main`) and the review CLI action path (`apg.review_cmd.review_action`). This is a DELIVERY-semantics choice, not a claim that those files are unscannable. TypeScript is already a scanned language: every `opencode-suite/tools/*.ts` is a File node with `code_type src` (e.g. `opencode-suite/tools/apg_review_action.ts`) alongside Struct nodes such as `scanner-optimisation.opencode-suite.lib.apg.ToolContext`. Markdown becomes a scanned language under `requirements.requirement.markdown-frontend`: once `.md`/`.markdown` are accepted, `opencode-suite/agents/*.md` enter the graph as File/section nodes. The code-FQN universe keys off Module/Struct/Function/File records with no `status` set (src/main.rs:1342-1364), independent of file extension, so a scanned `.ts` or `.md` File FQN is a LEGITIMATE `implemented-by` target. The anchor deliberately stays on the embedding/install Rust because the embedded constant is what the installer delivers (see `solution.note.markdown-anchoring` / `solution.note.embedded-template-anchor`).

Coverage caution for the plan-writer: the tier-4 delta is prose/template text embedded by a top-level `include_str!` constant that has no graph node; a plan task can only target a resolvable code FQN, so this component's anchors are delivery-path anchors. If the spine-scoped coverage gate demands a branch-added solution node's FQNs be touched, the plan should claim the install/action anchors it genuinely realizes rather than invent an edit to unchanged code.
